mappings.rationale: The criterion requires managing encryption keys across generation, distribution, storage, rotation, revocation and destruction with restricted access; CRY-09 is the cryptographic key management control covering exactly that lifecycle and the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the keys.

The four points of focus are capturing security events, protecting log integrity, retaining logs and reviewing them; MON-03 defines log content sufficient to establish what occurred, MON-08 protects event logs from unauthorised modification and deletion, and MON-01.8 is the ongoing review of event logs with escalation of incidents.

The criterion requires developing continuity plans addressing critical processes and RTO/RPO, testing them periodically and updating them from test results and change; BCD-01.7 is the formal BC/DR plan, BCD-04 the periodic exercise that confirms effectiveness, and BCD-06 the update of plans as people, process, technology and threats change.

The entity must warn users ahead of planned downtime and keep them updated during unplanned outages; CHG-05 ensures stakeholders are made aware of and understand the impact of proposed changes, covering planned downtime notice, and BCD-01.6 communicates recovery status and restoration progress to internal and external stakeholders during an outage — SCF has no status-page control, so the third point of focus is uncovered.

Access to confidential information must be restricted to individuals whose job requires it and reviewed periodically for appropriateness; IAC-20 enforces logical access permissions conforming to least privilege and IAC-17 is the periodic review that validates the need for each privilege and removes what is unnecessary.
